text: The visuals you'll use constantly. Let's start with the most common one of all: the column chart.

Give it a real date hierarchy, and four drill icons appear. Drill up moves to a higher level. Drill down lets you select one column to see its detail. Next level expands every column at once — no clicking through one at a time.

Select a data point, and it can affect other visuals two ways. Cross-filter hides unrelated data entirely. Cross-highlight dims it instead, keeping the full picture visible while emphasizing your selection.
And just like tables, chart colors can be data-driven — a gradient here, shading lower values red and higher values blue, performance visible at a glance.
Line charts for trend, pie charts for a small part-to-whole breakdown — same principles, different shapes. Next: cards, KPIs, and slicers — the visuals for single numbers and on-canvas filtering.
